THEY MUST MERGE AND DEPLOY TOGETHER — the SPA reads membershipRoleId, the two gallery channel ids and approvedBy off the new projections. *** THE HEADLINE: approve() WROTE THE MEMBER ROW AND ENQUEUED NOTHING. *** Enlistment was the one rank-assigning path in the app that never called a role sync, so an approved recruit got the rank on the dashboard and NO Discord role for it — it only landed later, by accident, on the next rank/medal change or a manual /discord/resync. *** THE SECOND HEADLINE: the JOIN ROLE meant the opposite of what the regiment wanted. *** It was handed to every account that walked into the guild, so a visitor who had never applied held exactly what an enlisted member held, which is why it could not be used as the one role channel permissions hang off. It is now `membershipRoleId`, granted from ROSTER STATE by reconcileRoles and NOT on join. RENAMED, not replaced: the live row already pointed at the `Member` role, so the migration carries the configuration across — a new column would have shipped NULL and granted nobody anything until someone noticed. WATCH THIS ON DEPLOY: reconcileRoles no longer exempts that role from stripping, so any guild member holding the old join role who is NOT an enrolled member loses it on their next reconcile. That is intended, but it is a real role removal against real people the first time the bot runs with syncRolesOnChange on. Visitors with no member row are never reconciled at all, so their stale grant is NOT cleaned up and needs a manual sweep in Discord. TWO BUGS THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH AND A LIVE CHECK DID (T-0200, T-0201): (1) the settings editor posts the WHOLE object on every save, so re-validating an unchanged membershipRoleId made one already-stored privileged role refuse the entire panel — channels, welcome copy, every toggle — naming a field the admin had not touched, and the bad value could not even be cleared because the clear posts the same body. Only a CHANGED id is validated now. (2) MediaEmbedService.resolve strips a leading `www.` before matching, and the new share service did not, so every `www.youtube.com` URL — the form YouTube's own share button produces — unfurled as plain text. Both now have tests; the YouTube one is parameterised over all four host forms. THE CADDYFILE IS THE ONE THING CI DOES NOT SHIP. Until that is done the /api/share/gallery/:id route works but https://lordsofholdfast.com/gallery/<id> still does not unfurl. A Caddyfile syntax error takes the whole site down (caddy is the only container with published ports) and recreating it must not lose the caddy-data volume (Let's Encrypt certs). LATEST SESSION (T-0190): the entry rank is now FROZEN against rename and delete. PR #52 -> dev, CI green, status `review`; flip to `deployed` once merged and shipped. Coupled frontend: lords-regiment-dashboard PR #47 (T-0277) — merge THIS one first, the SPA reads `isProtected` off the rank projection. *** THE HEADLINE: approve() resolved the entry rank BY NAME, so `Recruit` was a dependency wearing a label, and NOTHING stopped an edit_ranks_medals holder from renaming or deleting it. *** The delete half was not covered by the existing holder guard at all: remove() blocks a rank that is still held, but the entry rank is empty exactly when a regiment has no current recruits — on the dev stack Recruit reports holdersCount 0, so the FK RESTRICT would NOT have stopped it. Both refusals are 403 for EVERY caller including the Owner, deliberately not gated on a capability (same reasoning as MemberRole.Owner not being assignable through the API). WATCH THIS: only a CHANGED name is refused. The admin console posts the whole rank body on every save, so rejecting the mere presence of `name` would have blocked an icon or precedence edit on Recruit — there are tests on both sides pinning that. NO COLUMN, ON PURPOSE: the protected set is derived from the same ENTRY_RANK_NAME constant the enlistment path imports (src/ranks/protected-ranks.ts). A `protected` column would have defaulted to false on the live database and seedRanks is tier-2 greenfield-only, so it would never have been set there; deriving it in code also means the protected set cannot drift from the set of ranks the server actually depends on. Matching is CASE-INSENSITIVE because MySQL collation is: `WHERE name = 'Recruit'` already resolves a row stored as `recruit`, so a case-sensitive check would have left the row renameable to a variant the lookup still finds. NOTHING RESERVES THE NAME — a database that lost the row before this rule existed can recreate it, and an approval attempted meanwhile now fails with a 409 naming the rank to restore instead of a bare EntityNotFoundError 500. That path is reachable on any database renamed before this shipped; this PR freezes the row, it cannot un-rename one. tasks.title: Nightly database backups to R2 with a real restore drill
tasks.summary: Plan Phase 5. bin/lords-backup runs mysqldump --single-transaction --quick from inside the db container, through zstd, to r2:lords-backups via rclone, on a systemd USER timer at 03:30 UTC - deliberately before the 04:30 unattended-upgrades reboot window, with Persistent=true so a missed night runs on next boot. A user timer rather than a system one because linger is enabled and the deploy account already owns the docker socket and the .env, so backups need no root. It checks BOTH halves of the pipe: a mysqldump auth failure exits non-zero while still writing a short, perfectly valid .zst - exactly the backup that looks fine for months and restores to nothing. It also enforces an absolute size floor, refuses a dump more than 50% smaller than the largest stored one, and verifies the archive decompresses and ends with mysqldump's completion marker before uploading. The heartbeat is pinged ONLY on the success path, so the monitor alerts on its absence - the only way to catch the timer silently not running at all. bin/lords-restore-drill restores the newest backup into a scratch schema, diffs table and row counts against live, drops the scratch schema and prints the wall-clock time, which is the RTO. It is safe against production: it never writes to lords_dashboard.

tasks.title: Resolve event start/end in the event's IANA timezone instead of the process timezone

Existing wrong-time events are corrected by an admin re-saving them.
